headline: Report: Wild’s Faber clears return to play protocol, Spurgeon out week to week
take:
Daily Faceoff reports that Minnesota's Brock Faber has cleared return to play protocol after being out all regular season with a skull fracture, while Jared Spurgeon is out week to week with an undisclosed injury suffered during Tuesday's win.

So far this season, MIN is 9-3-2 and holds 59% of the expected goals, which measures the quality of chances each side creates. That is a strong underlying mark, and it comes with an oddity: the Wild's actual scoring is 12.6 goals below what their chances should have produced. Goals saved above expected, which shows how many more shots a goalie stops than an average one would, is +7.8, so the goaltending has covered for finishing that has lagged the chances. Faber's return would add to a team already controlling play, though the data gives us nothing on his own level this year.

Spurgeon's absence is the part to watch. The Wild's penalty kill allows 0.7 expected goals per game, and our data doesn't say who takes over his minutes, so we won't guess. We'd watch how the coaching staff handles the penalty kill and the top pair over the coming games.
